mechanism: The theoretical aggregation of all possible valid {{solver_tree}}s across all agents in the system. It represents the total epistemological state of {{problem}}-solving knowledge—the collective wisdom of self and others. Any specific problem-solving effort is a traversal or instantiation of a sub-graph within this Universal {{tree}}. It enables cross-agent learning: identifying redundant efforts, reusing proven {{solver_node}} strategies, and sharing {{solution}}s. The Universal Tree is the ground truth against which {{localized_learning}} updates are integrated.
gloss: Collective knowledge graph of all problem-solving
failure_modes: Fragmentation: Parts of the universal tree become inaccessible across agent boundaries.
Inconsistency: Contradictory solutions exist in different branches without reconciliation.
Knowledge Silos: Agent-local trees fail to sync with the universal tree.
invariants: Singularity: There is logically only one Universal {{tree}} containing all knowledge.
Coherence: Contradictions must eventually be resolved via synthesis or rejection.
